data.name: Amanvik
data.gender_notes: Amanvik is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aman means immortal or invincible, and vik means direction or path. Thus, Amanvik can be interpreted as the path to the immortal or invincible. The name Amanvik carries the meaning “Immortal, Invincible” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amanvik usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal, invincible and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner strength and resilience, encouraging one to face challenges with courage and determination.
data.etymology: Amanvik belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Immortal, Invincible.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amanvik total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Amanvik was a temple town in the medieval Bhakti period, located in the Western Ghats of present-day Maharashtra, India. It was a major center of the Vaishnavite Bhakti movement, with numerous temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu and his avatars. The town was also a significant cultural hub, attracting pilgrims, scholars, and devotees from all over India.

Amanvik is mentioned in the epic poem 'Ramayana' as the place where Sage Valmiki, the author of the poem, lived in penance and composed the epic. According to legend, Valmiki was a sage who had cursed King Dasharatha for not keeping his promise to the sage. The curse was that the king's son, Prince Rama, would die in exile. To atone for his mistake, Valmiki vowed to compose an epic poem to glorify Rama and his brother Lakshmana. He lived in Amanvik, meditating and composing the Ramayana.
